paper_title: Introduction to Computational Biology FT1 (2024-2025 ODD)

questions.question_text: Which of the following cell organelles does not contain DNA?
questions.answer: The nucleus, chloroplasts, and mitochondria all contain their own DNA, whereas lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain digestive enzymes and do not possess DNA.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not part of the cell theory?
options: All living things are made of cells.
Cells are the basic units of structure and function in all living things.
All cells contain the same organelles.
questions.answer: The main tenets of cell theory are that all living things are composed of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells. Different cell types contain different sets and quantities of organelles depending on their specialized functions.

questions.question_text: What is the small dark structure in the nucleus that produces ribosomes?
questions.answer: The nucleolus is a dense, spherical structure within the nucleus that is primarily involved in the synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and the assembly of ribosomes.

questions.question_text: What are the two proteins that Microtubules and Microfilaments are comprised of?
questions.answer: Microtubules are primarily composed of tubulin protein, while microfilaments (also known as actin filaments) are primarily composed of actin protein.

questions.question_text: Chitin is the compound present in the cell wall of which kingdom?
questions.answer: Chitin is a major component of the cell walls of fungi. Plant cell walls are primarily made of cellulose, while Monera (bacteria) have peptidoglycan and Protista are diverse, with some having cell walls of cellulose or other materials, but not typically chitin.

questions.question_text: Homeostasis usually returns the body to a healthy state after stressful stimuli by:
questions.answer: Negative feedback mechanisms are the primary means by which homeostasis is maintained. They work to reverse changes and bring physiological variables back to their set points.

questions.question_text: As blood glucose concentration decreases, what homeostatic response would the body produce?
options: Insulin would be released to cause blood glucose to fall.
Glucagon would be released to cause blood glucose to fall.
Insulin would be released to cause blood glucose to rise.
Insulin and glucagon would be released to cause blood glucose to rise.
questions.answer: When blood glucose falls, the body responds by releasing glucagon (not insulin) from the pancreas; glucagon stimulates the liver to break down glycogen and release glucose, so blood glucose rises back to its set point. Option B names the correct hormone; its statement that glucose 'falls' appears to be a misprint for 'rise', and the other options all involve insulin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be a negative feedback response by the body to hypothermia?
options: Vasoconstriction of blood vessels in the dermis
questions.answer: Hypothermia is countered by responses that generate or conserve heat: shivering, vasoconstriction of dermal blood vessels and an increased metabolic rate. These all oppose the fall in temperature (negative feedback). Sweating is a response to overheating, so it is not.

questions.question_text:
9. Match the following:
a. Receptor -
b. Stimulus
c. Control center -
d. Effector -
Produces response
Disruptions caused in control condition
Generates input
Receives input
questions.answer:
a. Receptor - Receives input
b. Stimulus - Disruptions caused in control condition
c. Control center - Generates input
d. Effector - Produces response

questions.question_text: Some of the body's homeostatic responses rely on “Positive feedback”. Which of the following happens in positive feedback?
options:
The body ignores changes in a physiological variable that are directed towards the set point for that
variable.

The body ignores changes in a physiological variable that are directed away from the set point for that
variable.
The body's response acts to oppose the change in the physiological variable.
The body's response acts to enhance the change in the physiological variable
questions.answer: Positive feedback loops amplify or intensify the initial change, moving the physiological variable further away from the set point, often leading to a rapid completion of a process (e.g., childbirth, blood clotting).
